rules.sentence: Eisenmenger syndrome (ES) is a constellation of symptoms that arise from a congenital heart defect and result in large anatomic shunts.
Ultimately, due to increased pulmonary vascular resistance, the left-to-right shunt will become a right-to-left shunt, resulting in significant hypoxemia and cyanosis.
PAH is a mean pulmonary arterial pressure greater than 25 mmHg while resting or 30 mmHg when exercising.
This may occur in large shunts or complex, unrepaired congenital heart disease as early as the first decade of life.
Eisenmenger Syndrome impacts many organ systems, often as a manifestation of chronic hypoxemia.[1]
